2609.27729.title: AI-Driven Neural Surrogates for In Silico Design of Cognitive-Affective Neuromodulation Targets
2609.27729.paper_summary: In neuropsychiatry, the primary goal is often not only to decode brain activity but to change it, for example to lessen a negative affective bias or an overly salient memory. Motivated by control theory, we develop an AI-driven neural-surrogate framework that proposes candidate representational changes and tests their predicted perceptual effects from snapshots of stimulus-evoked fMRI activity, without physical stimulation. The framework combines fMRI decoding, deep generative modeling, and constrained latent-space steering. Valence and memorability are used only as worked examples. Using more than 36,000 image-fMRI observations from four deeply sampled Natural Scenes Dataset participants, subject-specific models recovered coarse generative structure from visually responsive cortex (two-way identification, 0.79-0.88; chance, 0.5). Graded perturbations were reconstructed as images and evaluated with automated scorers and human ratings from 7,200 trials by 18 participants. In the primary VDVAE model, valence shifted from -0.61 to +1.03 SD and memorability from -1.34 to +1.45 SD; a later Versatile Diffusion refinement reduced or altered these effects. Across five perturbation levels, human valence ratings moved in the predicted direction under the linear time-correction model (mean slope, 0.038 SD per unit of alpha; 95 percent CI, 0.003-0.074; positive in 16 of 18 participants). Perceived memorability did not change reliably. Baseline agreement with the automated assessor was suggestive for valence (r = 0.30) and weak for memorability (r = 0.10). Extreme perturbations drifted from the original stimulus, so intended change must be weighed against loss of fidelity. These findings provide a falsifiable upstream method for designing and behaviorally testing candidate representational targets for future neuromodulation in psychiatry, while marking the limits of the present static approximation.
2609.27729.paper_summary_zh: 在神經精神醫學中，主要目標往往不僅是解碼大腦活動，而是改變它，例如減少負向情感偏見或過於顯著的記憶。受控制理論的啟發，我們開發了一個基於人工智慧的神經替代框架，該框架提出候選的表徵變化並測試其預測的感知效果，這些效果來自刺激引發的功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）活動的快照，而無需物理刺激。該框架結合了fMRI解碼、深度生成建模和受限潛在空間引導。價值和可記憶性僅用作示例。利用來自四名深度取樣自然場景數據集參與者的超過36,000個圖像-fMRI觀察，特定主題模型從視覺反應皮層中恢復了粗略的生成結構（雙向識別，0.79-0.88；隨機機率，0.5）。分級擾動被重建為圖像，並通過18名參與者的7,200次試驗進行自動評分和人類評價。在主要的VDVAE模型中，價值從-0.61轉變為+1.03 SD，而可記憶性從-1.34轉變為+1.45 SD；後來的多功能擴散精煉減少或改變了這些效果。在五個擾動水平中，人類的價值評分在線性時間修正模型下朝著預測的方向移動（平均斜率，每單位α 0.038 SD；95%置信區間，0.003-0.074；在18名參與者中有16名為正向）。感知的可記憶性並未可靠地改變。與自動評估者的基線一致性對於價值（r = 0.30）是有提示性的，而對於可記憶性（r = 0.10）則較弱。極端擾動偏離了原始刺激，因此預期的變化必須與保真度的損失進行權衡。這些發現提供了一種可證偽的上游方法，用於設計和行為測試未來精神病學中候選的表徵目標，同時標誌著當前靜態近似的限制。
